title: Matched single-arm studies built against one comparator arm
question: When several single-arm studies are each matched to the same comparator arm and their pseudo-contrasts enter a network as independent, how much does that overstate precision, and does it change the conclusion?
design: Network with two randomized trials and one to eight single-arm studies sharing one comparator arm; fixed-effect generalized least squares with the correct block covariance or with independence. 8 cells, 4000 replicates each.
answer: Entering pseudo-contrasts built against one comparator arm as independent counts that arm once per study. Its reported SE shrank as studies were added while the estimate's spread did not, so coverage fell from 0.88 with one study to 0.57 with eight (comparator arm of 50). Modeling the shared covariance kept coverage at 0.95. In this fixed-effect network the point estimate barely changed; the error is in the stated precision.
findings: Refuting sentence fails: naive coverage 0.567 to 0.884 with two or more pseudo-contrasts; correct 0.945 to 0.955.
Naive SE with a comparator arm of 50: 0.137 (one study) to 0.059 (eight), against a true spread of 0.167 to 0.147.
Mean absolute difference between naive and correct point estimates small; sign disagreement rare.
not_answered: Fixed-effect continuous network without a weighting step; heterogeneity and conflicting evidence, where the point estimate can also move, not run. Peer review has not been done.
estimand: A versus C mean difference in the network
methods_compared: generalized least squares with the shared-arm covariance
